'''Mariano Barbacid Montalbán''' (born 4 October 1949) is a Spanish molecular biochemist who discovered the first [[oncogene]] [[HRAS]].

== Early life and academic career ==
Barbacid was born in [[Madrid]], Spain on 4 October 1949.<ref name="elpais">{{cite news |url=http://www.elpais.com/articulo/sociedad/Barbacid/deja/direccion/CNIO/centrarse/investigacion/elpepusoc/20090929elpepusoc_15/Tes|title=Barbacid deja la dirección del CNIO para centrarse en la investigación|accessdate=29 September 2009|author=Javier Sampedro|date=29 September 2009|editor=El País|language=spanish|work=El científico ya expresó su intención de abandonar el cargo tras la puesta en marcha del centro oncológico}}</ref>

He completed his higher education in the [[Universidad Complutense de Madrid]], where he studied chemical sciences, and in the United States, where he started as an intern; years later he was appointed director of the Developmental Oncology Section of the Basic Research Program at NCI-Frederick, a center associated to the [[National Cancer Institute]]. He then moved back to his native Spain to lead the newly created [[Spanish National Cancer Research Centre|CNIO]] (Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Oncológicas). He also served on the Life Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] in 2011.{{citation needed|date=February 2026}}

== Scientific research ==
Barbacid is credited for isolating the human oncogene [[HRAS]] in bladder carcinoma. His discovery was published in [[Nature (journal)|''Nature'']] in 1982 in an article titled "A point mutation is responsible for the acquisition of transforming properties by the T24 human bladder-carcinoma oncogene".<ref name="T24">{{Cite journal |last=Reddy |first=E. P. |last2=Reynolds |first2=R. K. |last3=Santos |first3=E. |last4=Barbacid |first4=M. |date=1982-11-11 |title=A point mutation is responsible for the acquisition of transforming properties by the T24 human bladder carcinoma oncogene |url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7133135 |journal=Nature |volume=300 |issue=5888 |pages=149–152 |doi=10.1038/300149a0 |issn=0028-0836 |pmid=7133135}}</ref> He spent the following months extending his research, eventually discovering that such oncogene was the mutation of an [[allele]] of the [[Ras subfamily]], as well as its activation mechanism.

In 2003, he proved that the [[enzyme]] [[Cyclin-dependent kinase 2|CDK2]], until then believed to be indispensable in cellular division, was not necessary in order for [[DNA replication]] to take place.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12923533|title=Cyclin-dependent kinase 2 is essential for meiosis but not for mitotic cell division in mice|first1=Sagrario|last1=Ortega|first2=Ignacio|last2=Prieto|first3=Junko|last3=Odajima|first4=Alberto|last4=Martín|first5=Pierre|last5=Dubus|first6=Rocio|last6=Sotillo|first7=Jose Luis|last7=Barbero|first8=Marcos|last8=Malumbres|first9=Mariano|last9=Barbacid|date=4 September 2003|journal=Nature Genetics|volume=35|issue=1|pages=25–31|via=PubMed|doi=10.1038/ng1232|pmid=12923533}}</ref>

In December 2025, he published a paper in ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|PNAS]]'' describing a targeted therapy that successfully regressed [[pancreatic cancer]] and prevented tumor resistance in a mouse model.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2523039122|title=A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance|last=Barbacid|first=Mariano|date=December 2, 2025|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]|issue=49|volume=122}}</ref> This article was retracted on April 27, 2026 due to [[conflict of interest]] with its association to the company Vega Oncotargets, created to promote the drugs being evaluated.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Retraction for Liaki et al., A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance |url=https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2612385123 |journal=PNAS |volume=123 |article-number=18 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2612385123}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Expansión |date=2026-04-29 |title=La revista PNAS se retracta del estudio de Mariano Barbacid sobre cáncer de páncreas |url=https://www.expansion.com/directivos/estilo-vida/salud/2026/04/29/69f1b8c6e5fdea1d2c8b4595.html |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=EXPANSION |language=es}}</ref>  Barbacid claimed that "the value of my research is not in question" by the retraction and assured to resubmit his study with the required information.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Castro |first=Nuria Ramírez de |date=2026-04-28 |title=Barbacid se defiende tras la retirada de su estudio: «El valor de mi investigación no se cuestiona» |url=https://www.abc.es/sociedad/barbacid-defiende-tras-retractacion-estudio-valor-investigacion-20260428185354-nt.html |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=Diario ABC |language=es}}</ref> However critics stated that such procedure "it isn't a minor question".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Martínez |first=Javier Ruiz |date=2026-04-29 |title=Un catedrático avisa tras el artículo retirado a Barbacid: "Cuando uno no hace esa declaración de conflicto de intereses, de alguna forma está contaminando la ciencia" |url=https://cadenaser.com/nacional/2026/04/29/un-catedratico-avisa-tras-el-articulo-retirado-a-barbacid-cuando-uno-no-hace-esa-declaracion-de-conflicto-de-intereses-de-alguna-forma-esta-contaminando-la-ciencia-cadena-ser/ |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=Cadena SER |language=es-ES}}</ref>

In January 2026, Barbacid and his group at the CNIO published a study in which a combination of three targeted inhibitors, the established drugs [[afatinib]] and [[daraxonrasib]], and a compound used for cancer research named [[SD36 (PROTAC)|SD36]], showed promise in treating pancreatic cancer in animal models.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The group led by Barbacid at CNIO completely eliminates pancreatic tumours in mice with no resistance developing|url=https://www.cnio.es/en/news/the-group-led-by-barbacid-at-cnio-completely-eliminates-pancreatic-tumours-in-mice-with-no-resistance-developing/|website=CNIO|date=2026-01-29|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en-US|last=www.axel-k.com|first2=Pilar|last2=Gil}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euronews.com/health/2026/01/28/scientists-achieve-pancreatic-tumour-regression-in-breakthrough-study|website=Euronews|access-date=30 January 2026|title=Scientists achieve pancreatic tumour regression in breakthrough study|date=28 January 2026|last=Salido|first=Rafael}}</ref>

== Awards ==

His scientific career has been awarded with prizes such as the Distinguished Young Scientist Award (1983), the King Juan Carlos I Science award (1984), the Rhodes Memorial award (1985) and the Charles Rodolphe Brupbacher (2005). His effort has also been acknowledged with the Great Cross of the Order of 2 May (2011).

Other awards include:

* King Juan Carlos I Award (Spain, 1984)
* Rhodes Memorial Award (USA, 1985)
* Joseph Steiner Award (Switzerland, 1988)
* IPSEN Prize in neuronal plasticity (Austria, 1994)
* Charles Rodolphe Brupbacher Cancer Prize (Switzerland, 2005)
* International Agency for Research on Cancer Medal of Honor (France, 2007)
